newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MOTOR RACING-SICK VILLENEUVE FASTEST IN PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SICK VILLENEUVE FASTEST IN PRACTICE.

text.p: Jacques Villeneuve made light of illness and speculation about his future to set the fastest time in Friday's opening practice for the Argentine Grand Prix.
The Canadian had been forced to struggle with a stomach upset amid rumours that he may be leaving to set up his own team in the future and that he has already re-signed for Williams for 1998.
But a measured performance on the tight and twisty Autodromo Oscar Galvez showed Villeneuve was unconcerned by the rumours as he outpaced Brazilian Rubens Barrichello in a Stewart.
However, his team chief Frank Williams was angry and disappointed at reports which suggested he had re-signed the world championship favourite for next year and refused to confirm the stories.
"I have no comment to make at all," he told reporters at the track on Friday.

Villeneuve's manager Craig Pollock also dismissed the speculation in which he had been linked as an intermediary in the creation of a new team for 1999 backed by British American Tobacco (BAT) using Reynard chassis.
"We denied all this stuff in Brazil two weeks ago," he said. "This report is just off the pace. That's all there is to say about it. Nothing was happening then and it is the same thing here."
Whatever Villeneuve felt about it all, he was not allowing it to affect his driving on Friday.
His time of one minute 25.755 seconds shattered the track record set by Jean Alesi a year ago by nearly four seconds. He was on new tyres when he set his time.
"It's looking good for qualifying," Villeneuve said. "But we still have a lot of work to do for the race set-up. I am pleased that there was a new tyre lap there and that the car was good on it.
"We need to work on the race set-up for the longer runs to ensure that we are competitive. I am sure that there is still a lot of time to come out of the car."
Equally notable was the speed of the Bridgestone-tyred cars driven by Barrichello and Olivier Panis in his Prost.
This was the first example this year of the Japanese tyres securing such good positions on the opening day.
